 Old Farmer’s Almanac Christmas Weather Forecast 2026 for North America, Region by Region
 Brent Glogau | November 1, 2026 | Weather 
 Share this article 
 -->
 What will the Christmas forecast look like where you live? Credit: Kelly Canyon Ski Resort

 – daily powder forecasts for your ski area – 
 The Old Farmer’s Almanac released its 2026 White Christmas forecast for the United States and Canada on October 30. 
 The forecast varies considerably across North America. Some neighboring regions have very different outlooks. Here is what the Almanac predicts for each region.
 Three U.S. regions are forecast to have a White Christmas: the Northeast, Intermountain region, and Alaska. Several other regions have a chance of seeing at least an inch of snow on the ground Christmas morning. The Pacific Northwest, High Plains, Lower Lakes, and Ohio Valley all have a chance of a White Christmas. The southern Appalachians also have a chance, although the northern part of the region is not expected to have one.
 Related: Snow, Rain or Sun? Old Farmer’s Almanac Thanksgiving Weather Forecast 2026, Region by Region 
 2026 White Christmas forecast for the United States. Credit: The Old Farmer’s Almanac. 
 White Christmas forecast 2026: Where Else Could See Snow? 
 Much of the country is not expected to have a White Christmas. The Atlantic Corridor, Southeast, Florida, Deep South, Upper Midwest, Heartland, Texas-Oklahoma, Desert Southwest, Pacific Southwest, and Hawaii are all forecast to miss out, not surprisingly. The Appalachians have a split forecast, with the northern portion not expected to have a White Christmas and the southern portion having a chance.
 Related: NOAA Winter Outlook Favors a Wet Winter for California, the Southwest and Colorado 
 Canada is forecast to have a white Christmas across much of the country 
 Not surprisingly, much of northern Canada is forecast to have a White Christmas. Yukon, the Northwest Territories, and Nunavut are all expected to have snow on the ground. The forecast also calls for a White Christmas across northern British Columbia, the northern Prairies, northern Ontario, northern Quebec, and northern Newfoundland and Labrador. Southern Canada has a more mixed outlook. Southern Quebec and the western part of southern Ontario are forecast to have a White Christmas, while eastern southern Ontario has a chance. Southern British Columbia also has a chance.
 Atlantic Canada has a split forecast. Eastern areas have a chance of a White Christmas, while western areas are forecast to have one.
 2026 White Christmas forecast for Canada. Credit: The Old Farmer’s Almanac.

 What Counts as a White Christmas? 
 A White Christmas does not necessarily mean snow falling on Christmas Day. According to the National Weather Service, it means at least 1 inch of snow on the ground on Christmas morning. That means a storm earlier in December could deliver a White Christmas, even if skies are clear on December 25.
 What Are the Historical Odds of a White Christmas? 
 The Almanac’s forecast differs from the historical odds of a White Christmas. NOAA’s map uses climate data from 1991 to 2020 to show the probability of having at least 1 inch of snow on the ground on Christmas Day. The highest historical probabilities are generally found across northern states and mountainous areas, while the odds are much lower across the South and parts of the West. These figures are long-term averages, not predictions for Christmas 2026.
 Related: What Are the Chances of a White Christmas Where You Live? 
 For a broader look at what winter could bring, see the 2026-2027 Winter Weather Outlook . 
 The Almanac’s White Christmas forecast is an early look at the holiday, and conditions can change as December approaches. For now, those dreaming of a snowy Christmas have the best outlook in the Northeast, Intermountain region, and Alaska. Everyone else will have to wait and see what Mother Nature delivers.
